Subject: Data residency & retention questions for Redwood hosted API

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. As part of our vendor assessment for Redwood's hosted API, our security team has a quick set of clarifying questions focused on data residency, retention, and deletion. Can you confirm the answers below or point us to any docs you prefer we read? We are evaluating for production use in the US region.

1) Where is request/response data stored for hosted API customers that choose US residency (region specifics)?
2) What is your default retention window for raw request/response payloads, logs, and audit trails?
3) What is the deletion workflow if a customer requests immediate purge of their data? How long until data is removed from primary stores and backups?
4) Do you use customer request/response data to train models or tune weights?
5) Are telemetry and logs (IP, API keys, usage traces) tied to request content and how long are those retained?
6) How is encryption handled (at rest, in transit)? Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
7) Can customers pin region for storage only (requests can still be served from nearest runtime) — how do you guarantee no cross-border copies?
8) Any compliance artifacts we can review (SOC 2 summary, dataflow diagram, deletion playbook)?

Appreciate concise answers and any timelines. We may follow up with a couple of examples.

Thanks,
Eli
Eli Torres
Security Engineer | Delta Analytics

Eli —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers mapped to your questions. I'm attaching a short SOC 2 summary and a dataflow diagram for the US-hosted control plane. If anything here needs more detail, we can schedule a quick call or I can open a support ticket for a deeper audit.

1) Region/storage: For customers who select US residency we persist request/response data and customer metadata in our US-only cloud tenancy (AWS us-east-1 or us-west-2 depending on availability). Control plane meta-data for billing/console is also US-hosted for these tenants.

2) Default retention: By default we retain raw request/response payloads (for debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring) for 14 days. Audit logs (access events, token usage) are retained for 365 days by default. Customers on our Enterprise plan can request custom retention windows (e.g., 0/7/30/90 days) via contract.

3) Deletion workflow: Customers can initiate a purge via API/Console or by opening a support ticket. Once a purge request is received we:
   - remove primary copies from active stores within 72 hours,
   - trigger background expunge jobs that remove data from indices and metadata references within 72–96 hours,
   - mark snapshots/backups for deletion; backup objects are normally garbage-collected within 30 days (we provide a contractual option to accelerate to 7–14 days for Enterprise).
We provide a confirmation proof-of-deletion report for the primary stores and object keys used to verify removal.

4) Model training: We do NOT use customer request/response data from the hosted API to train or fine-tune our models. We maintain a strict policy that only explicitly contributed training datasets (from opt-in programs or open-source datasets managed separately) are used for model training.

5) Telemetry/logs: Telemetry (API key, request timestamps, route, token usage, compute metrics) is retained and linked to tenant IDs but request bodies containing PII are not indexed into our long-term analytics by default. Audit trails are retained 365 days; ephemeral runtime traces used for debugging live requests are rotated after 7 days.

6) Encryption & KMS: All data in transit uses TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3. At rest, we encrypt using AES-256. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys (AWS KMS or BYOK/HSM integrations) for at-rest encryption in supported deployments. Key rotation policies and access logs are available for review in our KMS integrations.

7) Region pinning / cross-border: For US-residency tenancies we avoid cross-border copies for stored data. Some runtime metadata (health metrics, anonymized telemetry) may be collected in secondary regions for operational stability but is aggregated and does not contain raw request/response content. If a customer requires hard geographic isolation (no cross-border telemetry), we offer Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or an Enterprise residency commitment with explicit routing policies.

8) Compliance artifacts: Attached: SOC2-Summary-Redwood-2027.pdf and redwood-dataflow-Aug2027.png. We can provide our deletion playbook and timestamps/proof on request via a secured support ticket.

Eli —

Following up with the specifics you asked for:

- Snapshots/backup semantics: Our snapshots are object-store based and deletion is eventual. When a purge request is issued we immediately remove primary object references and mark the snapshot objects for GC; however, underlying immutable snapshots may still exist until the storage provider's lifecycle completes. In practice, primary deletion completes within 72 hours and the storage-level GC removes snapshot objects within 30 days. For Enterprise contracts we can provide a tighter SLA (7–14 days) and an object-level proof-of-deletion report.

- Telemetry and PII: Telemetry that crosses regions is aggregated usage/metrics only (request counts, latency percentiles, error rates). We do not replicate raw request payloads or user prompts to secondary regions. If a customer includes PII in the prompt it is stored only in the tenant's primary US tenancy and subject to the retention window described earlier; aggregated telemetry will not contain prompt contents.

- KMS / key rotation: For Enterprise KMS integrations, customers control key material and rotation. We surface key usage logs (KMS decrypt operations keyed to tenant) and can provide last 6 months of key usage logs on request (delivered via secured support ticket). Note that log retention and delivery follow our access-controlled process; we will redact operational metadata as needed per legal requirements.

I will open support ticket #34219 (linked) and add your team so we can produce a redacted deletion proof and the key-usage extract. If you need a signed addendum on deletion SLAs or an updated MSA clause for backup removal timelines, we can route that to legal.
